summary: Phase 1 Location backend tests: 21/22 PASS. One CRITICAL PRIVACY LEAK confirmed — GET /api/users/{user_id} returns raw user doc including suburb_lat & suburb_lng (lines 567-572 of server.py). Spec explicitly says single profile must strip coords. Additionally, GET /api/auth/me and the user payload returned by /auth/signup, /auth/login, /auth/demo-login (via _safe_user) all leak suburb_lat/suburb_lng. Public list /api/users (with and without radius) is SAFE — coords are stripped. Radius query returns distance_km (rounded 1dp), sorted ascending, excludes location_visibility=private users. /api/suburbs/search ranks prefix matches first (Mandurah, Manly before substring hits), handles empty q (empty list), clamps limit to 30 max, accepts postcode prefixes (2095→Manly). /api/suburbs/by-postcode/2026 returns both Bondi & Bondi Beach. /api/suburbs/nearest returns nearest known suburb with distance_km < 10 for Sydney coords. POST /users/{id}/location: 'Manly' persists suburb+postcode+state+coords+visibility=suburb (response body excludes coords ✓); unknown suburb falls back to free-text (no coords); prefer_not_to_say clears all location fields & sets visibility=private; 404 for unknown user. All regression endpoints green: /community/today, demo logins (frankie/maggie/joycey), /games/sudoku/daily, /games/spot/daily, /admin/policy.

critical.issue: PRIVACY LEAK — returns suburb_lat & suburb_lng in the response. Spec says single-user profile must strip coords (publicly safe profile). Repro: POST /api/users/{frankie_id}/location {suburb:'Manly'} then GET /api/users/{frankie_id} → response contains 'suburb_lat': -33.7969, 'suburb_lng': 151.2871. Fix: server.py:567-572 — pop suburb_lat/suburb_lng before returning.

PRIVACY LEAK — these endpoints return the user dict via _safe_user() (or current_user dep) which strips _id/password_hash/lockout fields but NOT suburb_lat/suburb_lng. Same coord values reachable through self-auth. Confirmed via curl: /auth/me for frankie returns suburb_lat=-33.7969, suburb_lng=151.2871. Fix: update _safe_user() at server.py:292-299 to also pop suburb_lat & suburb_lng (and apply same projection to current_user). Same dict is the canonical 'user' object shipped to the client on every login — if cached locally it persists raw coords on the device.

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL): /api/users/{user_id} must strip suburb_lat & suburb_lng before returning. Easiest: replace the find_one projection with a projection that excludes those fields, OR pop them post-fetch. Recommended: build a shared `strip_private_location(user)` helper and use it in BOTH list_users (loop) and get_user.

FIX (CRITICAL): _safe_user() should also pop suburb_lat & suburb_lng so /auth/me, /auth/signup, /auth/login, /auth/demo-login don't leak coords on the wire. Verify current_user dependency (server.py:71-80) projection too.

Suggested defence-in-depth: factor a `PUBLIC_USER_PROJECTION = {'_id':0,'password_hash':0,'suburb_lat':0,'suburb_lng':0,'failed_login_attempts':0,'lockout_until':0}` and reuse across every user fetch.

After fix, re-run pytest backend/tests/test_location_privacy.py — the failing test test_single_profile_does_not_leak_coords should turn green. Also add `assert 'suburb_lat' not in user` to /auth/me & /auth/login test paths in next pass.

Note: Frankie's location was set to 'Manly' during the test; teardown restores it. If the failing test interrupted teardown for some reason, run: POST /api/users/{frankie_id}/location with {prefer_not_to_say:true} to reset.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:567-572 (get_user) uses {'_id':0} projection only — every other user field including coords is returned. This is the root cause of the critical leak. Contrast with list_users (server.py:543-564) which explicitly pops suburb_lat/lng — that inconsistency is exactly the bug.

_safe_user (server.py:292-299) is the canonical sanitiser for auth response payloads but lacks coord stripping. Any new sensitive field added in future will hit the same hole; consider an allowlist projection rather than blocklist popping.
set_user_location response (server.py:1109-1110) correctly returns only the public_keys subset — good pattern; please mirror this on the get endpoints.

list_users radius branch (server.py:538-559) correctly: (a) requires suburb_lat/lng to be set, (b) excludes location_visibility=='private', (c) computes distance_km, (d) pops coords, (e) sorts by distance. Solid.
suburbs.py search_suburbs ranks prefix=0, postcode-prefix=1, name-contains=2, needle-contains-name=3 — verified prefix-first for 'man' (Mandurah & Manly).
suburbs/nearest does a linear O(N) scan over ~140 entries — fine at this scale. If the dataset grows, consider precomputing a KD-tree.

POST /users/{uid}/location validates suburb name against the dataset; unknown names fall back to free-text storage WITHOUT coords — verified, this prevents poisoning the radius index with arbitrary lat/lng from client.

rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE: get_user at server.py:567-572 does `db.users.find_one({'id': user_id}, {'_id': 0})` and returns the raw dict. No coord-stripping. Meanwhile list_users took the trouble to pop coords (line 543-564) and set_user_location returns a curated public_keys subset (line 1109-1110), so the privacy contract WAS understood — get_user was simply missed. Same root cause for _safe_user — it strips auth secrets but not the newly-added location fields. MITIGATION: Introduce one shared sanitiser used by all 'return a user to a client' code paths (list_users loop, get_user, _safe_user, current_user dep) that pops both legacy secrets and any future location fields. Allowlist projection is safer than blocklist for this class of bug.
